setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Named repeatedly by both parties despite no title suffix. Rep: 'I've already heard a good amount of things from Kim' and 'I heard from Kim that you've been doing kettlebells for like a week now, right?' Prospect: 'I got messages from Kim' and 'Yeah, Kim, I have one from Kim, Richard.'

prospect.name: Dale H.
prospect.occupation: Not asked. Leaves the house around 6am and returns between 4 and 6pm; served in the military previously.
prospect.family_status: Not married; two sons aged nine and ten who play football
prospect.training_background: Lifting weights since he was very young, plus boxing and running; has never worked with a coach or trainer. Self-describes a compulsion to train daily leading to overtraining and injury. Switched to kettlebells one week before this call after finding Trevor on YouTube — owns one 35 lb kettlebell and has been doing two of Trevor's free videos four times a week plus a daily mobility video, at home.
prospect.medical: Extensive and undiagnosed. Hip, lower back, shoulder and knee pain that he rates 4-5 out of 10 and which he says has been worsening over the last couple of months — 'my body feels like it's falling apart'. Numbness and tingling in the left hand. Bad sciatic pain he attributes to heavy squatting. A previous left shoulder injury he links to the weakness and tingling. Runner's knee. Lower back, hip and knee pain triggered by time on his feet; shoulder pain and weakness triggered by working out. His stated fear is a wheelchair or a hip replacement by his fifties. No doctor, physio or other clinician is mentioned anywhere in the call, and none was asked about.

signals: Lost ground to a hard season of accumulated injury and wants function back: 'within maybe the last couple of months, my body feels like it's falling apart'
Regret about how he got here: 'I've always done things on my own... And I feel like I'm paying the price now with my body'
Motivated by return to a former capability rather than a new peak: 'I'd like to continue to run around with my sons'

Counter-signal considered and rejected: he is not the_medically_constrained, because no clinician has ruled anything out — nobody has assessed him at all — and price, not the body, is what stopped the sale

goals.text: Fix the mobility problems and get out of daily pain
Move well rather than just being strong — 'not just be a bodybuilder and be all stiff and uncomfortable'
Keep running around with his sons as they grow up and as he ages
Put on muscle and get lean
Avoid a wheelchair or a hip replacement in his fifties
Pass on what he learns to his sons — 'I'd be able to teach them the stuff that I learned'
Be held back from overtraining and taught to do less, correctly

pains.text: Hip, lower back, shoulder and knee pain rated 4-5 out of 10, worsening over recent months, requiring him to sit down for relief
Numbness and tingling in the left hand, linked to a prior shoulder injury
Sciatic pain attributed to heavy squatting, plus runner's knee
Compulsion to train every day leading to overtraining and repeat injury — 'mentally I need it, and then I end up over-training, and I end up getting injured'
Never had professional guidance in decades of training — 'I've always done things on my own'
Nightly ice cream binges — 'Last night I ate a whole pint' — undermining the fat loss goal
Fear of accelerating decline — 'I really don't want to be in a wheelchair when I'm in my 50s or have to get a hip replacement'
Tight budget with dependants — 'with life expenses and all of that, my budget is really tight' and 'I also got to make sure I have money to take care of my family'

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, so as much as I would like to do this, I don't even have the $6,000 to pay.
objections.rep_response: Ran the money play properly — isolated it ('outside of the investment, is it just the investment that's stopping you?'), then took monthly surplus ($400-500), savings (about $6,000) and credit score (740-750) — and then proposed third-party financing over twelve months at roughly $500 a month.

objections.raw_quote: This is something I kind of need to think about. I mean, I really want to do it, but I also got to make sure I have money to take care of my family.
objections.rep_response: Reassured him he was not being asked to spend food money, then ran the worth test twice, separating the outcome from the timing: 'do you feel like that outcome is worth six grand to you if you do it now or in a year?'

objections.raw_quote: I mean, I want to think, yeah, I'm just not willing to invest that kind of money into it right now.
objections.rep_response: Accepted the no on the core offer, confirmed he still wanted to act, then presented Primal University as a fallback and finally floated an unbuilt $3,000 six-month one-to-one tier as the reason to stay in touch.

objections.raw_quote: I'm optimistic that this is what I'm looking for. It's just something new. So, I mean, I'm excited, but I'm also nervous at the same time, because it's something I've never done.
objections.rep_response: Ran the fear play cleanly using his military service as the analogy — 'when you went in there, were you like 100% sure this is the right thing?' — and reframed nervousness as appropriate rather than disqualifying.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Third-party financing spread over twelve months at approximately $500 per month, proposed live after the credit score was disclosed. The rep characterised it as 'not like you take out a loan or anything, but then you do it through a third party'. No provider, rate or terms were named. Primal University was then offered as a lower-cost fallback, and an unbuilt $3,000 six-month one-to-one tier was floated as a future option.

evidence: IMPORTANT SCORING NOTE — the close rule was deliberately NOT applied here, and a mechanical reading of the transcript would misclassify this call. Both of its conditions are literally present: the prospect verbally agreed ('What do you say? Let's get started?' — 'Yeah, yeah, for sure', 00:28:16) and a payment link was sent and received ('Yeah, I just got the link', 00:29:06). But the agreement was retracted three minutes later, in the same recording, before any payment: 'as much as I would like to do this, I don't even have the $6,000 to pay.' The rule exists for calls that cut off before payment confirms; this one did not cut off.
Explicit refusal of the core offer: 'I'm just not willing to invest that kind of money into it right now'
Intent remains live: 'do you feel like that is something you still want to do?' — 'Yeah, for sure. It definitely is something I want to do.'
No decision was reached on either fallback. He agreed only to look: 'I'll look at his website and see what that university thing is and I'll make a decision.'
A further contact was agreed around an unbuilt cheaper tier: 'let's get in contact again a couple of days from now'
The Trevor onboarding call could not be scheduled — the only offered slots were 7:15am and 10:45am Hawaii time, both during his working hours
outcome.next_step: Prospect to review Primal University on the website and decide; rep to re-contact in a few days about a $3,000 six-month one-to-one tier he says Trevor is building.

notable.note: Three things a principal needs to see. First, clinical: a 36-year-old presenting with worsening multi-site joint pain, sciatica and numbness and tingling in his left hand — with no doctor, physio or clinician mentioned at any point — was taken through a full close for a loaded kettlebell programme, and nobody asked whether he had been assessed. Second, financing: after learning his monthly surplus is $400-500, the rep proposed third-party financing at roughly $500 a month for twelve months, which is effectively his entire disposable income, and described it as 'not like you take out a loan or anything'. Third, pricing: a $3,000 six-month one-to-one tier that does not exist was used as the reason to stay in contact, described as 'basically the exact same' as the $6,000 offer.

quality.notes: Persistent inversion of short turns from the first line onward — the call opens with the prospect's label carrying the rep's greeting, and the rep's own questions appear under 'Dale H.' at 00:00:46, 00:03:02, 00:05:38, 00:06:58, 00:10:12 and 00:22:17, while the prospect's answers appear under the rep at 00:03:48 and 00:19:11. The verbal agreement at 00:28:16 is itself split across labels. Roles resolved from content throughout. There are also several unintelligible passages where the audio drops ('19th... thing It's about... is... over').
